chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashshar, from a man, who raised it (to the Imam).

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Men whom neither merchandise nor selling diverts from the Remembrance of Allah,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are the merchants whom neither business nor selling diverts them from the Remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When the timings of the Prayer enter, they deliver to Allah His Right with regards to it.'
ai.seo_question: How do pious merchants balance business with prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific nature of the 'merchants of God' mentioned in Surah An-Nur, defining them not merely by their profession but by their disciplined adherence to prayer times amidst commercial activity. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating worldly livelihood with spiritual mindfulness, where the fulfillment of Salah serves as the primary metric of their devotion. This interpretation reinforces the concept that true piety in trade is demonstrated through the punctuality and sincerity of one's worship.
